about: Reference KAT list for the Korean KpqC algorithms SMAUG-T, NTRU+, HAETAE and AIMer. For each parameter set it lists the pinned reference versions (and known variants) with the SHA-256 of the source archive and of the .rsp file, a normalized digest of the whole file and one digest per record. A .rsp that matches tells which reference version's KAT it agrees with. This is not a certification: there is no official KpqC test programme, and it is not a substitute for KCMVP.

normalization.parse: Lines may end in LF, CRLF or CR. Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are skipped. Other lines are 'key = value'. Keys are trimmed and lower-cased. count, mlen, smlen and siglen are decimal integers written without leading zeros; every other value is hex, upper-cased. A count line starts a new record. Records keep file order.
normalization.record_digest: SHA-256 of the lines 'key=value\n' of one normalized record, keys sorted.
normalization.rsp_digest: SHA-256 of the lines 'record_digest\n' in file order, so it can be recomputed from record_digests alone.

keys.id: algorithms.<alg>.params.<id>: canonical parameter id, e.g. smaug-t/mode3. aliases are spellings seen in the reference code, Bouncy Castle and KpqClean_ver2; alias_seen_in says where.
keys.role: reference: a published reference version. known-variant: seen in a third-party library, matches no reference version.
keys.latest: true for the newest reference version of that parameter set.
keys.rsp_path: path of the .rsp inside the source zip, or inside the repository for a source without a zip.
keys.sizes: bytes of pk, sk and ct, ss (KEM) or sig (signature; for AIMer sig = smlen - mlen).
keys.differs_from: for each other version of the same parameter set, how many of the 100 records differ in each field.
keys.also_at: other places that publish the same .rsp bytes (same git blob SHA-1).
keys.excerpt: file under scan/kat/ with the first records, or null when the source may not be redistributed.

excerpt.decision: First 5 records (count 0 to 4) of every reference version and parameter set, all fields. 10 records would be 5014110 bytes; 5 records would be 2488276 bytes; the limit is 3000000 bytes. Plain JSON, not gzip: the wheel, the sdist and git compress it anyway. Known variants without a license (Bouncy Castle) have digests only.

smaug-t.name: SMAUG-T
notes: The official page asks for 1.2.0 and says 1.1.1 has implementation bugs. Every pk, sk, ct and ss differs between the two.
modet is TiMER (Tiny sMaug using Error Reconciliation), a security level 1 set with a shorter ciphertext.

The KAT program calls crypto_kem_keypair_internal(d, seed) and crypto_kem_enc_internal(mu) with d, seed and mu drawn from the NIST DRBG, in the same order as crypto_kem_keypair and crypto_kem_enc draw them.

ntruplus.name: NTRU+
notes: Parameter sets 768, 864 and 1152 only. 576 is a round 2 leftover and is not listed.
crypto_kem_dec returns 1 and sets ss to all zero bytes when decapsulation fails (no implicit rejection), as the reference kem.c says.

haetae.name: HAETAE
notes: Fields are siglen and sig (the signature alone), not the NIST smlen and sm.
1.1.2 and 1.2.0 give the same seed, msg, pk and sk. Only sig differs (1.2.0 changed the hyperball sampler).

The KAT program signs with a context string that the .rsp does not print: after the key seed it draws rnd (32 bytes), then ctxlen (1 byte) and ctx (ctxlen bytes) from the NIST DRBG and signs with pre = ctxlen || ctx. Checking a KAT signature with crypto_sign_verify needs that ctx.

aimer.name: AIMer
notes: Fields are smlen and sm, where sm = msg || sig.
The f and s sets use the same .rsp file names (PQCsignKAT_48.rsp, _72, _96), so the folder decides the set.
V3.0 (AIM3) changed pk, sk and the signature size from the 2026-01 package (AIM2).
The Bouncy Castle 'Round 2' KAT has the same pk and sk as the 2026-01 package (AIM2) but every signature differs. It matches no reference version and is listed as a known variant.
The KAT program signs with an empty context (ctx NULL, length 0). The reference implementation is little-endian only.
